name: Clark Tang
summary: Clark Tang is named in 2 Parts of The Buildout, most recently Part 16: The Seller Holds the Paper. Argued in Part 16 (The loan is a bridge).

parts.headline: Power Doesn’t Depreciate. Its Premium Moves.

mentions.excerpt: Clark Tang of Altimeter says hyperscalers retain an advantage through investment-grade balance sheets: they can build ahead of demand and rent at spot rates, while lenders finance neocloud hardware only against contracted offtake.

Clark Tang wrote in Key Context on August 12 that the new third-party money, from Apollo to KKR, was underwritten independently and takes the place of Nvidia's balance sheet, his answer to the circularity charge.

sides.claim: On circularity fears: recent third-party capital from Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR was independently underwritten apart from one another and replaces Nvidia's balance sheet rather than merely extending it, which…

Hyperscalers retained one structural advantage over neoclouds: investment-grade balance sheets that let them fund speculative capacity ahead of demand and rent it out at higher spot rates, whereas neoclouds could only get financing for hardware…
